title: Design a Rate Limiter
summary: Implement token bucket, fixed window, sliding window log and sliding window counter behind one interface, and be able to say what each one gets wrong — starting with the boundary burst that lets a fixed window pass double its limit.
concepts: Memory versus accuracy trade-offs between limiting algorithms
The fixed-window boundary burst, and two ways to fix it
Lazy token refill so idle clients cost nothing to track
Passing time in as a parameter so time-based logic is testable
Bounding per-client state so the bucket map is not a leak
extensions: Distribute the limiter across servers using Redis
Support different limits per customer tier
Limit on several keys at once (user, IP and endpoint)
Decide whether to fail open or fail closed when the limiter is unavailable
Emit standard X-RateLimit and Retry-After headers
